| `footing.fields` | NEW | describe door — one line under the fields region (variant B) | Your draft will be built to fill these 8 fields. | ⚠ STATES A COUNT, so in build it must be derived from the list rendered directly above it and never hardcoded. A hardcoded 8 beside a list of 5 is exactly the class of silent lie this phase exists to remove. |
| `footing.none` | NEW | describe door — same line, `none` arm (variant B) | This template has no fill-in fields, so your draft will be written from your description alone. | ⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT STRING ON THIS PAGE. SEED-158 says the plain-language client template is the COMMON case. Without this line the author attaches a real template, reads a sentence about it, and is never told the draft ignored it — SEED-157 recurring with a control on screen. It states the CONSEQUENCE ('written from your description alone'), never merely the fact. |
| `footing.notWord` | NEW | describe door — same line, `not-word` arm (variant B) | We can only read fields from Word documents, so your draft will be written from your description alone. | Separate from `footing.none` for the same reason the shipped sentences are separate: two of the three accepted upload types land here, and telling a .pptx author their deck has no fields would be a flat lie. |
| `footing.unavailable` | NEW | describe door — same line, `unavailable` arm (variant B) | We could not read this template's fields, so your draft will be written from your description alone. | ⚠ MUST NOT MERGE WITH `footing.none`, mirroring the shipped rule one level up. `none` is a fact about the document; this is a fact about us. The sentence promises the draft will use the template; nothing today stops the author pressing Draft before the read returns. |
| `cta.toFields` | CHANGE | testid="describe-draft" (variant C) | Write the first draft to these 8 fields | ⚠ CHANGES A GOVERNED STRING. The shipped CTA is "Write the first draft", carried in doorVocabulary.ts and settled by the operator as variant D of sketch 164 — three weeks ago. Variant C reopens it. It also makes the button's width depend on a number read from a document, which is a layout consequence, not just a copy one. |
| `cta.fromDescription` | CHANGE | testid="describe-draft" (variant C, all three no-fields arms) | Write the first draft from your description | Same cost as above. Its virtue is that the promise lands on the control the author is about to press rather than in a line they may not read; its risk is that a button which changes its own verb reads as two different actions. |

## The open question this sketch does NOT settle

**The `loading` arm is a race.** Nothing prevents the author pressing the draft button
while the read is in flight, which sends a generate call with no `template_placeholders`
and produces the blind draft this phase exists to prevent — on a screen that just told
them a template was attached. Three answers, none drawn: disable while reading · let the
draft wait for the read · let it through and reconcile afterwards (sketch 167).
**This belongs in CONTEXT.md as a decision, not inside a chosen variant.**
